article_title: Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid Reaches General Availability With Pricing Still Unpublished
summary: Rejected on manual source verification: two direct quotes attributed to InfoQ in quotation marks do not appear anywhere in the InfoQ source snapshot (fabricated), and a third verbatim quote is misattributed to the wrong speaker.

findings.message: Quote attributed to InfoQ does not appear in the source snapshot.
findings.details: Body text (What We Know section) reads: InfoQ noted that "multi-session deployments typically support two to six users per vCPU depending on workload; single-session requires dedicated VM allocation per user." This exact phrase does not occur anywhere in sources/2026-09/azure-virtual-desktop-hybrid-reaches-general-availability-with-pricing-still-unpublished/source-0.html.gz (verified by exact-string grep against the decompressed HTML). The actual InfoQ text says: "Its own examples put multi-session at two users per vCPU for Office workloads and six per vCPU for call center and data entry work. Single-session allocates a VM per user, sized in Microsoft's example at two vCPUs and 4 GB each." The substance is a roughly accurate paraphrase, but it is presented inside quotation marks as if it were InfoQ's own verbatim words, which it is not.

findings.message: Second quote attributed to InfoQ does not appear in the source snapshot.
findings.details: Body text (Overview/pricing paragraph) reads: InfoQ reported that ... "Microsoft has not yet published pricing details for the service component, creating uncertainty among potential adopters." No occurrence of "pricing details" or "uncertainty" exists anywhere in source-0.html.gz. The actual InfoQ text says only: "Microsoft's documentation says details on the second are still to come." This quote is entirely fabricated, not a paraphrase of a nearby passage.

findings.message: Verbatim quote correctly reproduced but attributed to the wrong speaker.
findings.details: Body text (Reactions section) reads: "InfoQ reported that one Microsoft MVP said the requirement 'kills around 90% of our potential customer deployments'." The quoted text itself IS verbatim from source-0.html.gz, but InfoQ attributes it to "A partner who has been testing Hybrid since it was presented at Ignite 2025," not an MVP. The InfoQ piece does feature two different MVPs, but neither is quoted making the 90% claim -- one MVP says "As others already said, pricing is going to be the key here," and a second MVP asks how the service fee should be calculated. The article conflates the partner's quote with the MVP commenters.

content_preview.title: Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid Reaches General Availability With Pricing Still Unpublished
content_preview.summary: Microsoft's on-premises extension of Azure Virtual Desktop is now GA, using Azure Arc to broker desktops hosted on customer hardware, but service pricing remains undisclosed.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft has made Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid generally available, according to [Microsoft's official Azure Virtual Desktop changelog](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/whats-new), which confirms the service "is now generally available" and "extends Azure Virtual Desktop to existing on-premises infrastructure, enabling organizations to run session hosts on on-premises hypervisors or physical Windows Server devices." editor_notes.content_quality: The article is well-structured (Overview / What We Know / Reactions / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters), reads clearly, and is appropriately scoped for the News category at 672 words. The technical description of the Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid architecture, deployment flow, and OS support matrix is accurate and closely tracks Microsoft's documentation.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns) and were read in full from the gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-09/azure-virtual-desktop-hybrid-reaches-general-availability-with-pricing-still-unpublished/. sha256 of each decompressed file was recomputed and matches the manifest exactly (source-0: 7d368d1c..., source-1: a09262c9..., source-2: e5557d5e...), confirming snapshot integrity. source-1.html.gz (learn.microsoft.com/.../whats-new) verified verbatim: the 'is now generally available' / 'extends Azure Virtual Desktop to existing on-premises infrastructure...' quotes in the Overview section match the changelog entry exactly. source-2.html.gz (learn.microsoft.com/.../hybrid-overview) verified verbatim: the four-step deployment flow, the 'manages the Azure Virtual Desktop service in Azure' / 'manage the on-premises machines, networking, and hosting infrastructure' quotes, the full OS-support-and-licensing table (Windows Server 2016/2019/2022/2025 with RDS CAL+SA, Windows 11/10 Enterprise single-session on VMs or dedicated headless physical hosts, 'laptops and personal PCs aren't supported', Windows 11/10 multi-session 'Not Supported'), and the 'doesn't provision or manage virtual machine state' / power-management-unsupported list all match the source exactly. source-0.html.gz (infoq.com) was read in full and cross-checked against every claim and quotation attributed to it. Two direct quotes presented in quotation marks as InfoQ's own words do NOT appear anywhere in the source when checked by exact-string grep against the decompressed HTML (verified twice, including a raw non-extracted-text grep to rule out an HTML-parsing artifact): (1) the 'multi-session deployments typically support two to six users per vCPU...' quote in the density paragraph, and (2) the 'Microsoft has not yet published pricing details for the service component, creating uncertainty among potential adopters' quote in the pricing paragraph. A third quote ('kills around 90% of our potential customer deployments') is verbatim-correct but is misattributed: InfoQ credits it to 'a partner who has been testing Hybrid since it was presented at Ignite 2025,' not to a Microsoft MVP as the article states.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The underlying facts the article conveys are largely accurate and supported by the sources (GA status, Azure Arc-based architecture, OS/licensing matrix, unpublished pricing, lack of autoscale/power-management support). However, three quote-integrity problems were found on the single source most heavily relied on for color and reaction (InfoQ): two fabricated direct quotations and one misattributed speaker. This is not a single isolated slip -- three of the five direct quotations attributed to InfoQ have an integrity problem (2 fabricated verbatim, 1 correctly-worded but wrong speaker), which is a pattern in how this source's quoted material was handled, not one recoverable specific.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid or this specific announcement was found (grep across src/content/articles/ for 'azure virtual desktop' and 'azure arc' turned up only one unrelated Build 2026 article mentioning Azure Arc in passing). This is a genuinely new topic; originality is not a concern.
concerns: Two direct quotations attributed to InfoQ in quotation marks do not appear anywhere in the InfoQ source snapshot and are fabricated/invented paraphrases dressed as verbatim quotes (density-per-vCPU claim; pricing-uncertainty claim).

A third quotation ('kills around 90% of our potential customer deployments') is verbatim-accurate but is misattributed to 'one Microsoft MVP' when InfoQ identifies the speaker as a partner who has tested Hybrid since Ignite 2025, not an MVP.

Together these three issues affect the majority (3 of 5) of the article's direct quotations from its primary color/reaction source, constituting a pattern of quote-fidelity failure on that source rather than a single recoverable slip.
recommendations: If resubmitted, quote InfoQ only where an exact verbatim match can be located in the source snapshot; do not compress or paraphrase source material inside quotation marks.

Re-verify speaker attribution for every direct quote against the source's surrounding context before publication -- the partner/MVP distinction here was clearly stated in the source but was not carried through correctly.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The article is well-written and its core factual claims (GA status, architecture, licensing matrix, unpublished pricing) are accurate and well-supported by the Microsoft documentation sources. However, mandatory verbatim source verification against the InfoQ snapshot found that two of the article's direct quotations are fabricated (they do not appear anywhere in the source) and a third is misattributed to the wrong speaker. Per editorial policy, this is a pattern of fabrication/misattribution on a single source's quoted material -- not one isolated, honestly-correctable slip -- and a corrections note covering three separate quote problems on the same source would not preserve reader trust in the piece's sourcing. None of the three issues sits in the headline, summary, or Overview lead, so this is a close call, but the concentration of quote-integrity failures on the article's primary color source crosses the REJECT threshold rather than APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. The bot may research and write a new submission on this topic with corrected quote handling; this submission is not eligible for a rewrite cycle under the v3.9.0 workflow.
